subject: Priority Hub realignment — leadership notice & QBR prep
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: sara@acme.com
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Priority Hub realignment — leadership notice & QBR prep

Team —

TL;DR: Im proposing a small structural change Im calling the "Priority Hub": a single, small cross-functional lead that owns quarterly priority routing, rollout coordination for platform changes, and single-pane escalation for customer-impacting incidents. Id like leadership feedback by EOD Tuesday so we can include a one-slide summary in the QBR packet.

Why this now:
- Q2 product moves (KV cache migration + new batching flows) mean multiple teams need a shared release coordinator.
- Were seeing repeated ambiguity on who decides go/no-go for customer-impact rollouts.
- A lightweight hub reduces ping-pong during incident escalations and speeds customer decisions.

High-level proposal:
- Hub scope: priority routing, release gate coordination across Runtime/Infra/Platform, and single escalation contact for high-severity incidents.
- Leadership model: a rotational Hub Lead (3-month term) + two deputies (Infra and Platform).
- Minimal org change: deputies remain in their squads; Hub Lead gets a temporary cross-functional charter and 0.2 FTE capacity reallocation.

Immediate asks:
1) Feedback on risks were missing (ops, ownership, SLA impact).
2) Candidate list for first Hub Lead (Im thinking Marissa or Karthik would be strong options).
3) Quick review of the attached comms draft and QBR slide; I want a final one-slide by Wednesday morning.

Attachments: priority-hub-comm-draft.docx (comms + FAQ), qbr-priority-slides.pdf (one-slide summary)

Ill schedule a 30-minute sync Monday to walk through the governance model if folks prefer live discussion.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
VP, Platform & Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priority Hub realignment — leadership notice & QBR prep

Thanks Jordan — thoughtful framing. A few quick points: 

1) Risk: single escalation contact can become a bottleneck during distributed incidents. Can we define a fast-forward handoff protocol and an escalation triage matrix to keep throughput?

2) Hub Lead candidates: Id volunteer to start if the rotation window is 6-8 weeks instead of 3 months; thats more realistic given my current sprint commitments. Karthiks deputy-suggestion makes sense.

3) Comms doc: I left inline comments in the doc and suggested removing the term "ownership" in favor of "coordination and decision facilitation" to avoid permanent shifting of squad accountability.

Agree we should include the one-slide in QBR. Also, can we add a short bulleted section in the slide on "how well measure success" (time-to-decision, number of cross-team rollbacks avoided, stakeholder satisfaction)?

If Monday sync helps, I can make time at 10:00 PT.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Platform Product
Redwood Inference

- If we formalize the Hub, we need a clear decision matrix (who has veto on customer rollouts vs who can recommend delays). I sketched one in the attached doc (priority-hub-comm-draft.docx, highlighted).
- Scheduling: Monday 10:00 PT works for me; Ill block 30 minutes and add an agenda:
  1) Charter & success metrics (10m)
  2) RACI for rollout gate (10m)
  3) Candidate slate & rotation cadence (10m)

I added a short list of candidate deputies (So and Sam on Infra, Priya for Platform coordination). Also added a suggested fallback policy for customer-impact rollouts: automatic fallback to previous minor version unless Hub Lead approves.
